cancer_indication: Hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative (HR+/HER2–) breast cancer; approved in advanced/metastatic settings in combination with endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant) and as monotherapy after endocrine and chemotherapy failure; also approved as adjuvant therapy (with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor) for high-risk, node-positive early breast cancer with Ki-67 ≥20%.
moa: Abemaciclib is a selective ATP-competitive inhibitor of CDK4 and CDK6 that arrests cell proliferation by enforcing the G1 cell-cycle checkpoint. It prevents RB1 phosphorylation, maintaining RB1 in its active state bound to E2F, thereby suppressing E2F target gene transcription and blocking the G1→S transition. In HR+ breast cancer, estrogen signaling upregulates Cyclin D1 (CCND1), activating cyclin D–CDK4/6 complexes; abemaciclib disrupts this ER→Cyclin D→CDK4/6→RB1→E2F axis and synergizes with endocrine therapy.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Gene set representing E2F-regulated transcriptional programs that drive DNA replication and S-phase entry.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation:
E2F output reflects the proliferative state governed by RB1; suppression of E2F targets is central to the cell-cycle control axis targeted by CDK4/6 inhibition in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In RB1-proficient tumors, CDK4/6-mediated RB phosphorylation releases E2F, inducing DNA replication genes (polymerases, MCMs, CDC6, etc.). Abemaciclib blocks RB phosphorylation, re-pressing E2F targets. Moderate to high E2F-target expression reflecting active but RB-dependent cycling tends to mark tumors that respond; extreme E2F activation via RB loss/c-MYC can bypass CDK4/6 and confer resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High E2F activity with intact RB1 reflects strong G1/S drive downstream of Cyclin D–CDK4/6; Abemaciclib blocks RB phosphorylation and shuts down E2F targets.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; MSigDB HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: When E2F hyperactivation is driven by RB1 loss or CCNE1/CDK2 overexpression, E2F remains active despite CDK4/6 blockade, so high E2F predicts poor benefit.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Pandey et al., Int J Cancer 2019, PMID 31025494.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Moderately low E2F in RB-proficient luminal tumors can still be further reduced by Abemaciclib, ensuring durable G1 arrest even if baseline proliferation is intermediate.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Neven et al., Breast Cancer Res 2021, PMID 33845788.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Very low E2F indicates quiescent/ER-independent biology or reliance on alternative survival programs, so E2F is not the key driver and CDK4/6 inhibition has limited impact.
Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A brief rebound of some E2F transcripts can occur as feedback during effective G1 arrest; if S-phase remains low and tumors respond, this remains a sensitive state.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Stable or rising E2F under Abemaciclib indicates escape from RB control (RB1 mutation, CDK6 or CDK2 upshift), a canonical acquired-resistance pattern.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Strong reduction in E2F targets is the desired PD readout of CDK4/6 inhibition and associates with durable G1 arrest and improved PFS/OS.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857; Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some resistant clones show E2F suppression but maintain survival via PI3K/AKT, Hippo/YAP or FGFR1, so cell-cycle transcription is no longer the main vulnerability.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.description: Gene set capturing early transcriptional responses to estrogen receptor signaling.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.interpretation:
Estrogen receptor signaling in luminal breast cancer upregulates proliferative programs including Cyclin D1, linking ER activity to CDK4/6-dependent G1 progression.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- ER signaling induces CCND1 (cyclin D1) and promotes CDK4/6 activity. Luminal ER⁺/HER2– tumors with intact ER signaling and dependence on estrogen-driven cyclin D1 show the greatest benefit from ET + CDK4/6i; ET plus abemaciclib suppresses ER target genes and cell cycle. Loss of ER or an “ER-low/non-luminal” phenotype associates with poorer CDK4/6i benefit.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High ER-early signature with intact RB1 reflects ER–Cyclin D–CDK4/6 coupling in luminal A/B tumors, making endocrine therapy plus Abemaciclib particularly effective.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Rugo et al., Oncologist 2019, PMID 31563959; MSigDB HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Very high ER signaling driven by ESR1 mutations and growth-factor crosstalk (FGFR1, PI3K) can drive endocrine resistance, so CDK4/6 inhibition adds limited benefit despite ER-high status.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635, doi:10.1038/s41467-019-09068-2; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Some ER+ tumors show dampened ER-early but still rely on ER–Cyclin D–CDK4/6; optimizing endocrine therapy and adding Abemaciclib can recapture control.
Asghar et al., ASCO PO 2022, doi:10.1200/PO.21.00002; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low ER-early signature often reflects ER-low/ER-loss or TNBC-like biology with growth-factor-driven proliferation, where Abemaciclib has minimal activity.
Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744; Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Under effective G1 arrest, some tumors show partial restoration of physiological ER feedback with ER-early upregulation while proliferation remains suppressed.
Conceptual ER-feedback extrapolation; Pandey et al., Int J Cancer 2019, PMID 31025494 (mechanistic review).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Marked ER-early rebound on Abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy suggests endocrine escape (ESR1 mutations, co-activator gain), with ER-driven proliferation resuming via Cyclin E/CDK2.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Chang et al., Anticancer Res 2023, PMID 38005037.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Concordant suppression of ER-early, E2F and cell-cycle signatures reflects effective blockade of the ER–Cyclin D–CDK4/6 axis and durable clinical benefit.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can progress despite low ER-early scores if they switch to ER-independent FGFR1, PI3K/AKT or Hippo/YAP drivers.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Sobhani et al., Cancers 2021, PMID 33535617.

REACTOME_CYCLIN_D_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_IN_G.description: Reactome pathway describing Cyclin D–CDK4/6-driven regulation of G1 progression through RB1 phosphorylation.
REACTOME_CYCLIN_D_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_IN_G.interpretation:
This pathway captures the core G1 control module frequently engaged in ER-driven breast cancers, where cyclin D–CDK4/6 activity is a major determinant of proliferation.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Overexpression/amplification of cyclin D1 (CCND1) or high CDK4/6 levels mark tumors that rely on this axis for RB phosphorylation and G1–S entry. Such tumors are particularly vulnerable to abemaciclib; pharmacologic CDK4/6 inhibition reduces pRb and arrests cells in G1.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High Cyclin D–CDK4/6 activity with RB1-proficient status creates archetypal CDK4/6-dependent G1/S progression, so Abemaciclib is highly effective.
Reactome R-HSA-69231; Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Pandey et al., Int J Cancer 2019, PMID 31025494.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Excess Cyclin D signaling with RB1 loss or CDK6 amplification can sequester drug and bypass RB control, reducing Abemaciclib’s ability to impose G1 arrest.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886; Papadimitriou et al., Cancers 2022, PMID 35595007.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Modestly low Cyclin D but intact RB1 can still represent Cyclin D-addicted clones where further suppression by Abemaciclib yields durable cytostasis, particularly in low-burden disease.
Asghar et al., ASCO PO 2022, doi:10.1200/PO.21.00002; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Very low Cyclin D suggests alternative drivers (Cyclin E/CDK2, PI3K/AKT, YAP/CDK6), producing intrinsic insensitivity to CDK4/6 inhibition.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: G1-arrested cells can accumulate Cyclin D transcripts transiently while RB remains hypophosphorylated; clinical sensitivity can persist.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Sustained Cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling during therapy marks selection for CDK6-high, YAP-driven clones that are refractory to Abemaciclib.
Liu et al., Biomedicines 2024, PMID 38371887; Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Strong reduction in Cyclin D–associated events is an expected PD effect of Abemaciclib and correlates with durable disease control in HR+ breast cancer.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Pandey et al., Int J Cancer 2019, PMID 31025494.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors may sustain growth via Cyclin E/CDK2, PI3K/AKT or YAP/CDK6 even when Cyclin D module is suppressed, so continued Abemaciclib has little effect.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.

REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_DURI.description: Reactome pathway describing Cyclin E–CDK2-mediated events controlling the G1/S transition.
REACTOME_CYCLIN_E_ASSOCIATED_EVENTS_DURI.interpretation:
Cyclin E–CDK2 provides an alternative mechanism to promote S-phase entry and can maintain G1/S progression independent of cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Cyclin E–CDK2 can maintain RB phosphorylation and drive S-phase entry even when CDK4/6 is inhibited. Clinical and translational data show high CCNE1 expression associates with short PFS and resistance to palbociclib/abemaciclib; low CCNE1 correlates with better outcomes.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Moderate Cyclin E–CDK2 activity can still depend on upstream Cyclin D–CDK4/6 priming; Abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy dampens both Cyclin D and subsequent Cyclin E activation.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong CCNE1/CDK2 overexpression is a classic bypass, enabling RB phosphorylation and S-phase entry even when CDK4/6 is inhibited.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Pandey et al., Int J Cancer 2019, PMID 31025494.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low Cyclin E/CDK2 with moderate Cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling implies that G1/S progression strongly depends on CDK4/6, making Abemaciclib particularly effective.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Asghar et al., ASCO PO 2022, doi:10.1200/PO.21.00002.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Very low Cyclin E signature may mark G0-like or persister cells where additional G1/S inhibition adds little clinical benefit.
Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Short-term compensatory Cyclin E upregulation can arise during effective G1 arrest without fully restoring RB phosphorylation; tumors can remain sensitive.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistently high Cyclin E–CDK2 activity on-treatment sustains proliferation and predicts poor outcome under ongoing Abemaciclib.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Pandey et al., Int J Cancer 2019, PMID 31025494.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Coordinated downregulation of Cyclin D and Cyclin E indicates deep G1/S blockade typical of strong responders to endocrine therapy plus Abemaciclib.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with suppressed Cyclin E, tumors can grow via PI3K/AKT, FGFR1 or Hippo/YAP, decoupling cell-cycle scores from clinical response.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.

REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.description: Reactome pathway describing dysregulated G1/S control in cancer caused by RB1 defects.
REACTOME_ABERRANT_REGULATION_OF_MITOTIC_.interpretation:
RB1 dysfunction removes a key tumor-suppressive checkpoint in breast cancer, leading to uncontrolled G1/S transition and altering the relevance of RB1-dependent cell-cycle control.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- RB1 is the canonical target of CDK4/6i. Tumors with RB1 loss-of-function (genomic loss, truncating mutation, complete protein loss) fail to undergo G1 arrest with CDK4/6 blockade and are essentially insensitive to abemaciclib. RB1 loss is a well-described mechanism of both de novo and acquired CDK4/6i resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Partial RB dysfunction with residual protein can leave some clones partially CDK4/6-dependent, giving transient benefit despite elevated RB-defect signatures.
Asghar et al., ASCO PO 2022, doi:10.1200/PO.21.00002; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High RB1-defect scores usually indicate functional RB loss and complete bypass of CDK4/6 control, predicting primary resistance to Abemaciclib.
Herrera-Abreu et al., Cancer Res 2016, PMID 27020857; McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low RB1-defect signaling implies intact RB; HR+/HER2– tumors with this profile are classic candidates for sustained benefit from Abemaciclib.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Rugo et al., Oncologist 2019, PMID 31563959; Asghar et al., ASCO PO 2022, doi:10.1200/PO.21.00002.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Even with low RB1-defect scores, activation of PI3K/AKT, FGFR1 or YAP/CDK6 can create CDK4/6-independent proliferation, driving resistance.
Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744; Chang et al., Anticancer Res 2023, PMID 38005037.

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible: On-treatment increase in RB1-defect signature implies expanding RB-deficient clones, which undermines RB-dependent CDK4/6 inhibitor action; durable sensitivity is not compatible with this pattern.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Rising RB1-defect signature during therapy signals outgrowth of RB-mutant/RB-low clones, a key mechanism of acquired CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance.
McCartney et al., Cancers 2019, PMID 31027341; Chang et al., Anticancer Res 2023, PMID 38005037.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Persistently low RB1-defect signaling on-treatment indicates preserved RB function and ongoing pharmacologic G1 control, consistent with continued sensitivity.
Asghar et al., ASCO PO 2022, doi:10.1200/PO.21.00002; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Lineage switching (e.g., towards basal-like phenotype) or alternative pathway dominance can drive progression despite low RB-defect scores.
Huang et al., Int J Mol Med 2022, PMID 36068886; Stanciu et al., Diagnostics 2023, PMID 36979744.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: Gene set representing PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity involved in growth, survival, and proliferation signaling.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation:
PI3K/AKT/mTOR is frequently activated in HR+ breast cancers and can sustain growth and survival programs that intersect with cell-cycle control and therapy response.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Activation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR supports cell growth and survival independent of cyclin D–CDK4/6, and is enriched in endocrine-resistant tumors. Functional proteomic and resistance-model studies show PI3K/AKT/mTOR upregulation in CDK4/6i-resistant breast cancer; dual CDK4/6 + PI3K/mTOR targeting can restore apoptosis and overcome resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Moderate PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation can still coexist with strong ER–Cyclin D–CDK4/6 dependence; such tumors may benefit from Abemaciclib up front and PI3K/mTOR inhibitors at progression.

Presti et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31540220; Abu-Khalaf et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2023, PMID 37507594; Hao et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38763709; MSigDB HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation (e.g., PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss) provides powerful growth/survival signals independent of RB/E2F and is a recurrent mechanism of de novo or early resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition.

Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Presti et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31540220; Dong et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33804268; Hao et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38763709; Targeting PI3K/mTOR after CDK4/6i: Breast Cancer Res 2020, PMID 32787986.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling with strong ER–Cyclin D dependence suggests that cell-cycle blockade by Abemaciclib alone is sufficient to produce a robust response in HR+/HER2– disease.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812; MSigDB HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some tumors with low PI3K/AKT/mTOR scores rely instead on alternative RTKs (e.g., FGFR1) or Hippo/YAP programs; lack of PI3K activity alone does not guarantee CDK4/6 sensitivity, and primary resistance can still occur.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846; Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Early feedback upregulation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR after G1 arrest can be partially compensatory; if cell-cycle signatures remain suppressed and disease controlled, Abemaciclib retains clinical activity.
Dong et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33804268; Presti et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31540220.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Clear on-treatment activation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR is a hallmark of acquired CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance; adding PI3K or mTOR inhibitors is a rational salvage strategy.
Breast Cancer Res 2020, PMID 32787986; Hao et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38763709; Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: When Abemaciclib-based therapy is combined with PI3K/mTOR blockade or tumors have weak survival signaling, both cell-cycle and PI3K/AKT/mTOR modules are suppressed, yielding deep and durable responses.
Dong et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33804268; Hao et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38763709; Breast Cancer Res 2020, PMID 32787986.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: In some late-stage clones, survival can be maintained via FGFR1, Hippo/YAP or immune evasion even when PI3K/AKT/mTOR and cell-cycle modules are pharmacologically suppressed, leading to progression with a low PI3K signature.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846; Zhao et al., Transl Cancer Res 2023, PMID 36774005.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_FGFR1.description: Reactome pathway describing signaling downstream of FGFR1 through MAPK and PI3K-related cascades.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_FGFR1.interpretation:
FGFR1 pathway activation promotes proliferative and survival signaling in breast cancer and can drive endocrine resistance and alternative growth signaling networks.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- FGFR1 amplification and MAPK activation induce cyclins and CDK6, providing an alternative proliferative drive that bypasses CDK4/6 blockade. In ER⁺ breast cancer, FGFR1-altered models and patients show resistance to ET + CDK4/6i, which can be mitigated by FGFR inhibitors.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Low–moderate FGFR1 signaling in ER+/HER2– tumors may coexist with dominant ER–CDK4/6 dependence; such cases can still derive meaningful benefit from Abemaciclib, with FGFR1 becoming more relevant at progression.
Mouron et al., Breast Cancer Res 2021, PMID 33691725; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Reactome R-HSA-190236.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: FGFR1 amplification/overexpression is a well-established driver of endocrine and CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance, activating MAPK and PI3K pathways and reducing reliance on CDK4/6-mediated RB control.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Sobhani et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33535617; Mouron et al., Breast Cancer Res 2021, PMID 33691725; Clin Cancer Res 2019, PMID 31340908.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low FGFR1 signaling indicates absence of this RTK bypass; ER+/HER2– tumors with FGFR1-low profiles are more likely to respond durably to endocrine therapy plus Abemaciclib without needing FGFR-targeted combinations.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some FGFR1-low tumors can still be resistant via PI3K/AKT activation, Hippo/YAP signaling or RB1 alterations, so low FGFR1 alone does not ensure CDK4/6 inhibitor sensitivity.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A slight on-treatment increase in FGFR1 signaling may reflect emerging subclones; if ER/RB dependence remains and tumor burden shrinks, Abemaciclib can still be clinically effective.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Sobhani et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33535617.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong upregulation of FGFR1 signaling under therapy is a prototypical acquired resistance mechanism, restoring proliferation via MAPK and PI3K despite CDK4/6 blockade.
Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635; Mouron et al., Breast Cancer Res 2021, PMID 33691725; Sobhani et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33535617.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Lack of FGFR1 activation together with effective G1 arrest supports continued Abemaciclib sensitivity with no evidence of RTK-driven escape.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: In resistant tumors FGFR1 may not be the dominant bypass; progression can occur via PI3K/AKT, YAP/CDK6 or immune escape even when FGFR1 signaling is low.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_P16_CELL_CYCLE_G1.description: KEGG Medicus reference pathway describing CDKN2A (p16INK4A) regulation of CDK4/6 and the G1/S transition.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_P16_CELL_CYCLE_G1.interpretation:
p16INK4A is a key regulator of the G1 checkpoint; its expression patterns reflect underlying RB1–CDK4/6 axis status and cell-cycle control states in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- CDKN2A/p16^INK4A^ normally inhibits cyclin D–CDK4/6. In many HR⁺ breast cancers, loss of p16 is part of the oncogenic program and may mark CDK4/6 dependence and sensitivity; conversely, high p16 frequently accompanies RB1 dysfunction or other cell-cycle rewiring, correlating with poor response to CDK4/6i in several datasets and xenograft models. Thus “p16 up” is generally a red flag for resistance when it reflects an abnormal RB loop.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Modest p16 upregulation with intact RB1 can reflect a partially engaged checkpoint that remains suppressible; Abemaciclib can still enforce a more durable G1 arrest in this context.
Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812; Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong p16 overexpression frequently accompanies RB1 loss; in this setting cells are G1/S-competent without CDK4/6, making high p16 a classic marker of primary resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low p16 with intact RB1 and high Cyclin D–CDK4/6 activity describes the canonical luminal phenotype, which is highly susceptible to Abemaciclib.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some resistant tumors maintain low p16 but proliferate via CCNE1/CDK2, PI3K/AKT or YAP/CDK6, effectively bypassing the p16–RB–CDK4/6 axis.
McCartney et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31027341; Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Mild p16 induction upon G1 arrest can act as secondary checkpoint reinforcement; if RB remains functional and proliferation is suppressed, tumors can remain Abemaciclib-sensitive.
Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812; Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Marked increase in p16 with progression usually reflects expansion of RB-deficient cells where p16 is uncoupled from G1 control, indicating resistance to Abemaciclib.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Persistently low p16 in RB-intact, Abemaciclib-treated tumors is compatible with continued reliance on CDK4/6 activity and sustained response.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Resistant clones may retain low p16 but proliferate through CDK2 or RTK/PI3K signaling; p16 downregulation does not preclude CDK4/6 inhibitor failure.
McCartney et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31027341; Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886.

KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_PDL_PD1_SHP_PI3K_.description: KEGG Medicus reference pathway describing PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint signaling via SHP phosphatases and PI3K-related signaling in immune contexts.
KEGG_MEDICUS_REFERENCE_PDL_PD1_SHP_PI3K_.interpretation:
This pathway represents immune checkpoint regulation that can shape the tumor microenvironment and antitumor immune activity relevant to breast cancer treatment responses.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- CDK4/6 inhibition (including abemaciclib) modulates the tumor immune microenvironment, increasing antigen presentation and T-cell infiltration but also inducing PD-L1 upregulation as a negative feedback. This PD-L1 increase is treatment-associated, not a classic baseline selection marker; it may limit long-term responses unless combined with immune checkpoint blockade. Upregulation is primarily post-treatment/adaptive (CDK4/6i-induced PD-L1 on tumor and immune cells)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Moderate PD-1/PD-L1 pathway engagement in HR+ tumors can coexist with Abemaciclib sensitivity and represents a setting where combining CDK4/6 inhibitors with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade may be particularly effective.
Schaer et al., Cell Rep 2018, PMID 29539425; Schaer et al., Cancer Res 2018 (Abstract 4569); Nayyar et al., Nat Commun 2024, PMID 38388416.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Strong PD-1/PD-L1–SHP–PI3K signaling can suppress antitumor T-cell responses and promote immune escape, limiting the overall effectiveness of Abemaciclib, especially when immune control is required.
Tzetzo et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2025, PMID 39901392; Dong et al., Cancers (Basel) 2021, PMID 33804268.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Low PD-1/PD-L1 signaling in a T-cell–inflamed microenvironment may permit Abemaciclib’s intrinsic antiproliferative effect plus its immunomodulatory actions (enhanced antigen presentation) to work optimally.
Schaer et al., Cell Rep 2018, PMID 29539425; Dowless et al., Clin Cancer Res 2018, PMID 30219755.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In “immune-cold” tumors, low PD-1/PD-L1 pathway activity often simply reflects absent T-cell infiltration; Abemaciclib’s immunologic benefits are muted and resistance is driven by tumor-intrinsic pathways.
Zhao et al., Transl Cancer Res 2023, PMID 36774005; Tzetzo et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2025, PMID 39901392.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: CDK4/6 inhibition can increase PD-L1 expression while enhancing antigen presentation and T-cell activation; higher PD-1/PD-L1 signaling on-treatment may accompany improved response when combined with checkpoint blockade.
Schaer et al., Cell Rep 2018, PMID 29539425; Schaer et al., Cancer Res 2018 (Abstract 4569); Wang et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2024, PMID 38735881.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If PD-1/PD-L1 upregulation occurs without sufficient T-cell activation or checkpoint inhibition, the net effect is immune escape and resistance to Abemaciclib-based regimens.
Yang et al., J Biomed Sci 2025, PMID 39899058; Tzetzo et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2025, PMID 39901392.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Successful combination therapy (Abemaciclib plus ICI and/or RT) may normalize or reduce PD-1/PD-L1 signaling while preserving a T-cell–inflamed phenotype, aligning with durable tumor control.
Schaer et al., Cell Rep 2018, PMID 29539425; Wang et al., Transl Lung Cancer Res 2024, PMID 38735881.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: With chronic therapy, both PD-1/PD-L1 signaling and T-cell infiltration may collapse (“immune desert” or exhaustion), leading to progression despite ongoing Abemaciclib.
Zhao et al., Transl Cancer Res 2023, PMID 36774005; Tzetzo et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2025, PMID 39901392.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_HIPPO.description: Reactome pathway describing Hippo tumor suppressor signaling controlling YAP/TAZ-driven transcription and proliferation programs.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_HIPPO.interpretation:
Hippo pathway integrity restrains proliferative signaling; disruption (e.g., via FAT1 loss) can increase proliferative drivers such as CDK6 and cyclins in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Loss of FAT1 impairs Hippo tumor-suppressor signaling, leading to nuclear YAP/TAZ accumulation and transcriptional upregulation of CDK6 and other proliferative genes. Functional genomics screens and clinical correlates in ER⁺ breast cancer show FAT1 and other Hippo alterations as recurrent drivers of CDK4/6i resistance.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Moderate Hippo pathway activity restraining YAP/TAZ can help limit unchecked proliferation; tumors may still rely on canonical ER–Cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling and respond to Abemaciclib.
Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846; Reactome R-HSA-2028269.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: If “up” reflects YAP/TAZ activation rather than canonical Hippo-mediated inhibition, YAP1-driven CDK6 upregulation and survival signaling can confer CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance even before treatment.
Li et al., Cancer Cell 2018, PMID 29657129; Li et al., Clin Cancer Res 2019, PMID 30559195; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Low YAP/TAZ oncogenic activity (effective Hippo suppression of YAP) leaves tumors more reliant on ER–Cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling and thus more vulnerable to Abemaciclib.
Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846; Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Some resistant luminal tumors may show low Hippo/YAP transcription but instead use PI3K, FGFR1 or RB1 alterations; low Hippo signaling alone does not ensure sensitivity.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Mild YAP transcriptional activation under therapy might initially coexist with ongoing RB-dependent G1 arrest; short-term Hippo/YAP increases do not always imply clinical failure.
Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846 (extrapolation).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Sustained YAP/TAZ activation induces CDK6 expression and pro-survival programs, providing a robust escape route from CDK4/6 inhibition and driving resistance to Abemaciclib.
Li et al., Cancer Cell 2018, PMID 29657129; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Suppressed Hippo/YAP signaling together with blocked G1/S transition describes a deeply controlled state where neither proliferation nor a YAP-mediated escape route is active, favouring durable response.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Li et al., Front Pharmacol 2020, PMID 33192846.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors may progress using PI3K/AKT, FGFR1 or immune escape even while Hippo/YAP remains transcriptionally low; Hippo downregulation alone is insufficient for control.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Formisano et al., Nat Commun 2019, PMID 30914635.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene set representing regulation of the G2/M checkpoint and mitotic progression programs.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation:
G2/M checkpoint and mitotic gene expression tracks overall proliferation programs in breast tumors and is coupled to broader cell-cycle activity states relevant to therapeutic control of growth.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- TK1 activity reflects S-phase flux and is downstream of CDK4/6–RB–E2F signaling. Patients starting CDK4/6i + ET with high baseline TK1 but showing a robust early decline in TK1 activity have better PFS; persistent or rising TK1 on therapy marks early progression. Thus TK1 is best viewed as a pharmacodynamic marker, with baseline high proliferation compatible with sensitivity but on-treatment decrease being the key favorable sign.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: High G2/M and mitotic activity often track with overall high proliferation; although CDK4/6 inhibitors act in G1, having many cycling cells entering the cycle can still favour benefit from G1 arrest by Abemaciclib in RB-intact tumors.
Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812; Tzetzo et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2025, PMID 39901392; MSigDB HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: In RB-deficient or Cyclin E–driven tumors, strong G2/M signatures reflect rapid cycling that is not rate-limited by CDK4/6; Abemaciclib fails to restrain these cells, resulting in functional resistance.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; McCartney et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31027341.

Sensitive: Mechanistically plausible: Lower G2/M activity in RB-intact luminal disease can still be adequately controlled by CDK4/6 inhibition, especially in indolent metastatic settings where modest blockade is sufficient to delay progression.
Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882; Goetz et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28968163; Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812.
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Very low G2/M activity may characterize dormant, senescent or non-cycling clones that are inherently insensitive to cell-cycle inhibitors, leading to limited impact of Abemaciclib.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Tzetzo et al., NPJ Breast Cancer 2025, PMID 39901392.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: A transient mitotic spike in a subset of cells can occur as populations re-synchronize; if overall proliferation indices fall and disease regresses, Abemaciclib can still be considered effective.
Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812 (extrapolation).
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Persistently high or rising G2/M signatures on-treatment suggest that cells have escaped G1 control and continue to cycle, indicating resistance to Abemaciclib.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; McCartney et al., Cancers (Basel) 2019, PMID 31027341.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Decreased G2/M checkpoint activity is a downstream readout of successful G1 restriction—fewer cells reach mitosis, consistent with tumour shrinkage or durable stable disease under Abemaciclib.
Glaviano et al., Cancer Treat Rev 2024, PMID 38452812; Sledge et al., JCO 2017, PMID 28580882.
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: When G2/M genes are suppressed but progression occurs through non-proliferative mechanisms (stem-like persisters, EMT, PI3K or YAP-driven survival), low G2/M no longer predicts sensitivity to Abemaciclib.
Huang et al., Front Oncol 2022, PMID 36068886; Li et al., Cancer Cell 2018, PMID 29657129.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: ER-positive (luminal) breast cancers often overexpress Cyclin D1 (CCND1) and rely on cyclin D–CDK4/6 complexes to phosphorylate RB1 and enable proliferation, indicating strong dependence on the CDK4/6-controlled G1 checkpoint.

High baseline CDK4 expression is described as a marker of dependence on cyclin D–CDK4/6 signaling, consistent with the central role of CDK4 in driving RB1 phosphorylation and G1→S progression in luminal breast cancer.
Abemaciclib’s antiproliferative effect depends on an intact RB1 pathway; functional RB1 enables suppression of E2F transcription and G1 arrest.
In HR+ breast cancer, estrogen signaling (ESR1 activity) upregulates Cyclin D1 (CCND1), maintaining engagement of the cyclin D–CDK4/6–RB axis that underlies cell-cycle progression.
A strong ER-driven luminal program (including ER-related gene expression such as PGR) is described as characteristic of ER+ tumors where the ER→Cyclin D→CDK4/6 pathway is engaged.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Cyclin E1 (CCNE1) overexpression or amplification is described as enabling cyclin E–CDK2 bypass of CDK4/6 inhibition; absence or low activity of this bypass is associated with greater reliance on cyclin D–CDK4/6 control.

High p16INK4A (CDKN2A) is described as indicating an aberrant RB regulatory loop and poor response contexts; by contrast, low p16 is described alongside intact RB axis states that align with effective G1 checkpoint control.
Declining thymidine kinase 1 (TK1) activity reflects suppression of S-phase/DNA synthesis after treatment and is described as an on-treatment marker associated with longer progression-free survival.

Lack of PI3K pathway hyperactivation is described as a context in which tumors rely more on the cyclin D/CDK4 axis, whereas PI3K activation is described as a route that can undermine reliance on CDK4/6-mediated control.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Amplification or overexpression of CCNE1 is described in clinical cases of CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance and provides cyclin E–CDK2 activity that can maintain RB1 phosphorylation and S-phase entry despite CDK4/6 inhibition.

FGFR1 pathway activation (including FGFR1 amplification) is described as driving downstream MAPK and PI3K signaling, inducing cyclins and CDK6, and being enriched in tumors progressing on CDK4/6 inhibitors.
FGFR2 alterations are described as occurring in patients who progressed on CDK4/6 inhibitors, consistent with activation of FGFR signaling as an alternative growth route.

PIK3CA-associated PI3K/AKT/mTOR hyperactivation is described as a bypass survival/proliferation route implicated in resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition and addressed in combination strategies that co-target PI3K.

Upregulation of CDKN2A (p16INK4A) is described in non-responder contexts and linked to an aberrant RB regulatory loop; p16 overexpression is described as correlating with poor response in ER+ xenografts.

CDK6 upregulation is described as a resistance mechanism, including selection for CDK6 amplification/overexpression during prolonged CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure and as a downstream consequence of FAT1/Hippo pathway loss.
Resistant cells are described as showing increased expression of MYC and broader proliferative transcriptional programs that can support cell-cycle progression under therapeutic pressure.
KRAS mutations are described as emerging in some metastatic HR+ patients after CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and activating MAPK signaling that can promote cell-cycle progression.
HRAS amplification is described as emerging in some metastatic HR+ patients post-CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and driving MAPK signaling as a resistance route.

ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) is described as an efflux transporter substrate relevant to abemaciclib exposure; increased ABCB1 expression is described in preclinical resistance models as reducing intracellular drug concentration.
ABCG2 (BCRP) is described as an efflux transporter substrate relevant to abemaciclib exposure, contributing to reduced effective drug levels in preclinical contexts and sanctuary sites.
Anti-apoptotic signaling (including BCL2) is discussed as a factor that can allow survival during cytostatic arrest, with combination strategies being explored to convert arrest into cell death.

MCL1 is discussed as a survival factor where downregulation (e.g., via BH3 mimetics) can convert CDK4/6 inhibitor-induced arrest into tumor cell death, indicating that strong survival signaling can reduce depth of response.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss-of-function RB1 mutations or deletions are described as eliminating the G1 checkpoint that CDK4/6 inhibitors enforce, producing primary or acquired resistance because G1 arrest cannot be induced without RB1.

Loss of FAT1 is described as downregulating Hippo tumor suppressor signaling, unleashing YAP-driven programs that increase CDK6 and cyclin expression and correlate with shorter progression-free survival on CDK4/6 inhibitors.

Downregulation or loss of estrogen receptor signaling is described as reducing reliance on ER-driven cyclin D1 programs and diminishing benefit because the clinical benefit of CDK4/6 inhibitors is confined to ER-positive disease.

Loss of TP53 is discussed as potentially weakening stable checkpoint responses (e.g., p21 induction) and durable suppression under CDK4/6 inhibition, contributing to intrinsic resistance in some subtypes.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B): The strongest evidence for efficacy and mechanisms comes from luminal subtypes. Luminal A tumors (ER+/PR+, low Ki-67) are described as highly sensitive and reliant on Cyclin D1–CDK4/6 with intact RB1; luminal B tumors also benefit, but resistance mechanisms such as CCNE1 amplification and PIK3CA mutations are described as more frequently observed. RB1 alterations are described as rare at baseline but can emerge as acquired resistance after progression; tumors with high Cyclin D1 and low p16 are described as very responsive; PIK3CA-mutant luminal cancers respond but may have shorter duration and PI3Kα inhibition can be effective post-resistance.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-positive/ER+ (Triple-positive): Abemaciclib is described as showing efficacy in ER+/HER2+ metastatic breast cancer when combined with HER2-targeted therapy and endocrine therapy, supported by phase II data (monarcHER). These tumors are described as still relying on cyclin D–CDK4; resistance may involve upregulation of HER2/MAPK signaling (if HER2 therapy is suboptimal) or PI3K pathway activation, and toxicity monitoring is noted due to combination regimens.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC): Not standard for TNBC, but certain subsets may derive benefit. RB1 wild-type TNBC with high RB expression and low p16 is described as having some sensitivity, while ~20–30% TNBC with RB1 loss or inactivation is described as lacking efficacy. The LAR (Luminal Androgen Receptor) subtype is described as potentially more responsive and under investigation; abemaciclib is described as having CNS penetration and being trialed in brain metastases; TNBC often requires combination therapies (e.g., with immune checkpoint blockade) to be effective.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA1/2-mutated or HRD+: Overlap mostly with TNBC or some luminal B cases; no direct contraindication described. HRD status is described as not clearly predicting CDK4/6 response and being orthogonal; some HRD+ tumors are basal-like (likely resistant due to RB1 loss), others luminal B (could respond). Data are described as limited regarding differential benefit by BRCA status.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Basal-like / Claudin-low: Described as typically RB1-deficient, p16-high, and highly proliferative (often TNBC) and generally poor candidates for CDK4/6 therapy, with expected rapid resistance via cyclin E upregulation or lack of effect due to absent RB.
